aria: Animated recap of the Mavericks' 120 to 101 win at Denver: Cooper Flagg's driving floater with 4:49 left that made it 106 to 88, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Flagg's 24 points and 12 assists, the top scorers, how the Mavericks won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from StatMuse's game page for the Mavericks' 120–101 win at Denver on Nov 24, 2026: all 120 Dallas points and all 101 Denver points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (48 of 98, 11 of 37 from three, 13 of 20 FT for Dallas; 34 of 85, 12 of 39, 21 of 24 for Denver), rebounds (48–41), assists (31–22), steals (13–6) and turnovers (12–18). The quarter scores (24–34–26–36 to 17–22–38–24) are also on the FOX Sports box score page; 58–39 at the half is in the AP, Field Level Media and Dallas Sports Journal, and 84–77 after three in Dallas Sports Journal and Denver Stiffs. Points in the paint (68–38) and fast-break points (35–7) are in the AP, Dallas Sports Journal and Fadeaway World. Dallas' biggest lead, 22, is in Field Level Media, Dallas Sports Journal and Fadeaway World; Denver's 5-point lead early in the first quarter is in the Denver Gazette and VAVEL. Flagg's 24 points, 12 assists (tying his career high, AP), 6 rebounds, 8 of 17 and 7 of 9 FT also match Dallas Sports Journal and Fadeaway World. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Tuesday's games.

Dallas has won four straight (AP; Field Level Media; Dallas Sports Journal) and is 3–0 in NBA Cup group play (Dallas Sports Journal); it clinches the group with a win at Phoenix on Friday or a Phoenix loss at Houston on Wednesday (Field Level Media; Denver Gazette). Denver scored 38 in the third quarter and got within 80–77 on DeMar DeRozan's three-point play with 1:11 left in it (AP; Dallas Sports Journal); Dallas then scored 13 of the next 15 points (Dallas Sports Journal). P.J. Washington returned after missing two games with an illness (AP; Dallas Sports Journal). Flagg's 11th 20-point double-double tied Dwight Howard for the second-most by a teenager (AP). Next: Dallas visits Phoenix on Friday (AP; Dallas Sports Journal); Denver visits Utah on Friday (AP; Denver Gazette).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Cooper Flagg's 9-foot driving floater with 4:49 left that made it 106–88: StatMuse's play-by-play has "C. Flagg makes 9' driving floater" at 4:49 for 106–88, after his two free throws at 5:14 made it 104–88; Field Level Media: Flagg's floater and free throws pushed the lead to 18. So the board's Mavericks +16 to +18 is 104–88 to 106–88. No assist is listed and the defender isn't described, so it is drawn as the template's plain drive to a short finish. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Dallas Mavericks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Flagg's listed 6-foot-9 and 205 pounds (RealGM; Wikipedia), with arms at the default length because neither reports a wingspan, in the Mavericks' road kit with No. 32 (RealGM; Wikipedia) and the default darker skin tone, since he has no approved look yet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
